audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for marriage, mutual conjugal authority, singleness gift, mixed marriage, call/condition, present distress, undivided devotion. Preserve pastoral counsel, not universal coercion.

verses.restored: Now concerning the things you wrote: It is beautiful/good for a human not to touch a woman.

familiar.text: Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote unto me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.

verses.restored: But because of sexual immoralities/misuses, let each man have his own wife, and each woman have her own husband.

familiar.text: Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.

verses.restored: Let the husband give to the wife what is owed, and likewise also the wife to the husband.

familiar.text: Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.

verses.restored: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband; likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.

familiar.text: The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.

verses.restored: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a season, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer, and then be together again, so that the adversarial one may not test you because of your lack of self-control.

familiar.text: Defraud ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency.

verses.restored: But I say this as concession, not as command.

familiar.text: But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment.

verses.restored: I wish all humans were as I myself am; but each has one's own gift from the Divine, one this way and another that way.

familiar.text: For I would that all men were even as I myself. But every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that.

verses.restored: To the unmarried and widows I say: it is beautiful/good for them if they remain as I also am.

familiar.text: I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, It is good for them if they abide even as I.

verses.restored: But if they do not have self-control, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.

familiar.text: But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn.

verses.restored: To the married I command, not I but the Lord: a wife is not to be separated from a husband,

familiar.text: And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband:

verses.restored: but if she is separated, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to the husband; and a husband is not to send away a wife.

familiar.text: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife.

verses.restored: But to the rest I say, I, not the Lord: if any sibling has an untrusting wife and she consents to dwell with him, let him not send her away.

familiar.text: But to the rest speak I, not the Lord: If any brother hath a wife that believeth not, and she be pleased to dwell with him, let him not put her away.

verses.restored: And if any woman has an untrusting husband and he consents to dwell with her, let her not send away the husband.

familiar.text: And the woman which hath an husband that believeth not, and if he be pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him.

verses.restored: For the untrusting husband is sanctified in the wife, and the untrusting wife is sanctified in the sibling; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

familiar.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy.

verses.restored: But if the untrusting one separates, let that one separate. The sibling, man or woman, has not been enslaved in such cases; in peace the Divine has called us.

familiar.text: But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.

verses.restored: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save/heal the husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save/heal the wife?

familiar.text: For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife?

verses.restored: Only, as the Lord assigned to each, as the Divine has called each, so let one walk. And thus I direct in all the assemblies.

familiar.text: But as God hath distributed to every man, as the Lord hath called every one, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all churches.

verses.restored: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not draw over. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

familiar.text: Is any man called being circumcised? let him not become uncircumcised. Is any called in uncircumcision? let him not be circumcised.

verses.restored: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping the commandments of the Divine.

familiar.text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.

verses.restored: Let each remain in the calling in which one was called.

familiar.text: Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called.

verses.restored: Were you called as enslaved? Do not let it trouble you; but if you are able to become free, rather use it.

familiar.text: Art thou called being a servant? care not for it: but if thou mayest be made free, use it rather.

verses.restored: For the one called in the Lord as enslaved is the Lord's freed one; likewise the one called as free is Messiah's enslaved one.

familiar.text: For he that is called in the Lord, being a servant, is the Lord’s freeman: likewise also he that is called, being free, is Christ’s servant.

verses.restored: You were bought with a price; do not become enslaved to humans.

familiar.text: Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men.

verses.restored: Siblings, in what each was called, let each remain with the Divine.

familiar.text: Brethren, let every man, wherein he is called, therein abide with God.

verses.restored: Now concerning virgins/unmarried ones, I have no command of the Lord, but I give judgment as one shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.

familiar.text: Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord: yet I give my judgment, as one that hath obtained mercy of the Lord to be faithful.

verses.restored: I think therefore this is beautiful/good because of the present necessity/distress: that it is beautiful/good for a human to be thus.

familiar.text: I suppose therefore that this is good for the present distress, I say, that it is good for a man so to be.

verses.restored: Have you been bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Have you been released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

familiar.text: Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? seek not a wife.

verses.restored: But if you marry, you did not sin/misalign; and if the virgin/unmarried one marries, she did not sin/misalign. Yet such will have pressure in the flesh, and I am sparing you.

familiar.text: But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh: but I spare you.

verses.restored: This I say, siblings: the season has been shortened; from now on, let those having wives be as though not having,

familiar.text: But this I say, brethren, the time is short: it remaineth, that both they that have wives be as though they had none;

verses.restored: and those weeping as though not weeping, those rejoicing as though not rejoicing, those buying as though not possessing,

familiar.text: And they that weep, as though they wept not; and they that rejoice, as though they rejoiced not; and they that buy, as though they possessed not;

verses.restored: and those using the world as not using it fully; for the form of this world is passing away.

familiar.text: And they that use this world, as not abusing it: for the fashion of this world passeth away.

verses.restored: I want you to be without anxiety. The unmarried man is anxious for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;

familiar.text: But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord:

verses.restored: but the married man is anxious for the things of the world, how he may please the wife,

familiar.text: But he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife.

verses.restored: and he is divided. The unmarried woman and the virgin are anxious for the things of the Lord, to be holy in body and spirit; but the married woman is anxious for the things of the world, how she may please the husband.

familiar.text: There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

verses.restored: I say this for your own benefit, not so that I may throw a noose upon you, but toward what is well-formed and devoted to the Lord without distraction.

familiar.text: And this I speak for your own profit; not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely, and that ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction.

verses.restored: But if anyone thinks he is acting improperly toward his virgin/unmarried one, if she is beyond prime and so it ought to happen, let him do what he wills; he does not sin/misalign; let them marry.

familiar.text: But if any man think that he behaveth himself uncomely toward his virgin, if she pass the flower of her age, and need so require, let him do what he will, he sinneth not: let them marry.

verses.restored: But the one who stands firm in his heart, having no necessity but having authority concerning his own will, and has judged this in his own heart to keep his virgin/unmarried one, will do beautifully/well.

familiar.text: Nevertheless he that standeth stedfast in his heart, having no necessity, but hath power over his own will, and hath so decreed in his heart that he will keep his virgin, doeth well.

verses.restored: So then the one marrying his virgin/unmarried one does beautifully/well, and the one not marrying will do better.

familiar.text: So then he that giveth her in marriage doeth well; but he that giveth her not in marriage doeth better.

verses.restored: A wife is bound for as long a time as her husband lives; but if the husband sleeps, she is free to be married to whom she wills, only in the Lord.

familiar.text: The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord.

verses.restored: But she is more blessed/flourishing if she remains thus, according to my judgment; and I think I also have Spirit of the Divine.

familiar.text: But she is happier if she so abide, after my judgment: and I think also that I have the Spirit of God.

translation_notes: Romans-style care continues: this chapter is pastoral counsel under present distress, not universal coercion.
Verses 36-38 are syntactically difficult and may refer to a betrothed daughter/ward or one's own betrothed; restored wording preserves ambiguity with virgin/unmarried one.
